messages:
Laura M.: Quick post-launch triage plan — we've got a backlog spike from launch + 3 customer asks. Proposal: pause new feature work for one sprint, allocate capacity to fixes, and run a short daily triage for the next 5 business days. Thoughts?

Sam K.: +1 on pausing new features. Suggest we define a simple bug vs enhancement rubric and a 'quick-win' tag for items that are <= 2 engineer-days. Also can we reserve a small canary pool for fixes only? @Kevin C. can you confirm infra?

Anil R.: From eng perspective: 50% capacity to fixes seems high for us this week — can we do 30% core + 20% on-call buffer (to handle surprises)? We should also define a rollback window for risky changes and require CI gating for any canary promotion. Quick triage labels below: 

```
/triage-priority
- P0: production outage / data loss
- P1: customer-impacting regression (signed customers)
- P2: functional bug with known workaround
- P3: polish / enhancement / UX tweaks
- quick-win: estimated <= 2 engineer-days
```

Maria T.: Product: we need to prioritize based on customer impact, not just severity. Signed customers > trials > internal. Please add a 'customer-impact' field to tickets (customer name + severity). Also propose an SLA for triage responses: P0 within 1h, P1 within 4h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Kevin C.: Infra: we have a dedicated canary pool we can reserve for hotfixes. I'll set an autoscale policy and a route for fix traffic. Daily 15-min sync at 10:30 PST works for me. I'll tag infra owners on canary ops. :thumbsup:

Laura M.: Ok — let's agree on the operational criteria. Proposed prioritization matrix (short version):

- Blocker (P0/P1) -> immediate patch + customer comms
- High (P2 impacting multiple customers) -> include in current sprint or hotfix window
- Medium (single-customer non-blocking) -> next sprint slot, owner assigned
- Low (P3/enhancement) -> backlog grooming

And quick rules:
- Quick-win -> onboard to current sprint if it doesn't bump a P0/P1
- WIP limit -> no more than 8 active bug tickets without explicit approval

Sam K.: I'll go tag current items in the backlog and mark 'quick-win' where applicable. Also suggest we create a short checklist on each ticket: reproduction steps, customer impact, rollback plan, owner.

Maria T.: Agree. Also ask DevRel to surface any community reports. We should add a small dashboard metric: regressions-per-release and median time-to-fix.

Anil R.: I'll add CI gating and the rollback template to the engineering runbook. Can we agree owners for the next 48h?

Laura M.: Owners: Sam K. = triage lead, Anil R. = eng fixes coordinator, Kevin C. = canary/infra lead, Maria T. = customer comms. I'll maintain the action list and assign tickets.

DeployBot: DeployBot: canary-deploy started for fix/1782 — 10% traffic on dedicated-fix-pool (sha: 2f9bcd).

Kevin C.: Noted. I'll promote to 50% on green, then full if metrics stable for 30m.

Maria T.: Customer comms draft ready, posting to #customer-updates for review.

Sam K.: Heads-up — I'll cap concurrent bug WIP to 8 and update owners on tickets now.

Laura M.: Thanks everyone. Action items: 
- Sam: tag backlog + triage lead (today)
- Anil: CI gating + rollback template (today)
- Kevin: reserve canary + autoscale (today)
- Maria: customer comms draft + dashboard metric (today)
I'll run the 10:30 PST 15-min triage tomorrow and each weekday for the next week. :rocket:
